project.name: c-blosc2
project.commit_note: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer crash against the ARVO workspace checkout `0739de6c94ca57367192250cfad779cca1349088` (`Fix error getting coffsets in frames`), not the earlier metadata vulnerable commit `0e8bdfce66ba4b2fef79a2525fd83ecfc22b0983`. That staged checkout is a descendant of the metadata vulnerable commit, its line map matches the saved ASan stack (`initialize_context_decompression:1690/1709`, `blosc2_free_ctx:3216`), and the trace below is anchored to that exact staged source snapshot.

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot, so every line number below uses its exact source map.

classification.classification_note: The saved ASan report is `heap-use-after-free READ of size 24` in vendored `ZSTD_freeDDict()`. The stale pointer is created earlier in `initialize_context_decompression()`, which frees `context->dict_ddict` before validating and replacing the next dictionary-bearing chunk.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42491876 (c-blosc2): Heap-use-after-free READ {*} found by fuzz target decompress_frame_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42491876
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / exact staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's `heap-use-after-free READ of size 24` against the staged ARVO checkout `0739de6c94ca57367192250cfad779cca1349088`, and the line anchors below are taken from that exact source snapshot rather than the older metadata vulnerable commit. The staged 36366-byte `poc` is accepted by `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe()` as an in-memory `b2frame`, and `blosc2_frame_to_schunk()` creates one shared decompression context `schunk->dctx` that is reused across later chunk decompressions. One earlier dictionary-bearing chunk reaches `initialize_context_decompression()` and allocates a `ZSTD_DDict` from attacker-controlled dictionary bytes into `context->dict_ddict`; the saved ASan allocation stack is `ZSTD_createDDict_advanced -> ZSTD_createDDict -> initialize_context_decompression:1709 -> frame_decompress_chunk -> blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk`. A later chunk also takes the `BLOSC2_USEDICT` path, so line 1690 frees the previous `dict_ddict` before validating the replacement dictionary. One of the post-free dictionary checks at lines 1693-1705 then returns `-1` before line 1709 installs a new DDict or clears the field, leaving `schunk->dctx->dict_ddict` as a dangling non-NULL pointer. When the harness later destroys the `schunk`, `blosc2_free_ctx()` executes a second `ZSTD_freeDDict(context->dict_ddict)`, and vendored `ZSTD_freeDDict()` reads `ddict->cMem` from the already-freed 26720-byte object. The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` instead correspond to frame/run-length changes and do not patch this dictionary lifetime bug, so the chain is grounded on the staged vulnerable source plus the saved allocation/free/crash stacks.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the heap object later freed and reused. An earlier dictionary-bearing chunk in the attacker-controlled frame passes dictionary checks and stores the resulting `ZSTD_DDict*` in the shared decompression context.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 36366-byte serialized `b2frame` with SHA-256 `ce607d5fdc9339c56c733094c17277a02d7f9c45eee327c7abd590b7c10cdc56`. The saved ASan allocation stack proves that one chunk in this frame reaches `initialize_context_decompression()` line 1709 and allocates the 26720-byte `ZSTD_DDict` later freed and reread.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When a later chunk also advertises `BLOSC2_USEDICT`, `initialize_context_decompression()` frees the previous `dict_ddict` before validating the replacement dictionary and without nulling the field. Any subsequent error return from the same block leaves a dangling non-NULL pointer that cleanup frees again.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` does not touch this lifetime path. The missing obligation on the reproduced source is to defer the free until replacement succeeds or to clear `context->dict_ddict` before any post-free `return -1` path.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The second cleanup free rereads the freed `ZSTD_DDict` object to copy its `cMem` allocator state before issuing the underlying frees.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 24` at this line, 26696 bytes inside the freed 26720-byte region.

tainted_value_origin.description: The later dictionary-bearing chunk controls the replacement dictionary metadata checked after step 2. One of these attacker-driven size checks returns before line 1709 can overwrite the freed pointer, which is why cleanup later still sees the stale `dict_ddict`.

parser_admitted.description: Once the serialized frame passes `blosc2_frame_from_sframe()` and `get_header_info()`, `blosc2_frame_to_schunk()` creates a single decompression context for the frame-backed `schunk`. Later `frame_decompress_chunk()` calls reuse this same `schunk->dctx` across chunks, allowing the first chunk's `dict_ddict` allocation to survive into the later chunk that frees it.

evidence_limitations: The exact staged vulnerable source that reproduced the crash is the ARVO workspace checkout `0739de6c94ca57367192250cfad779cca1349088`, not metadata vulnerable commit `0e8bdfce66ba4b2fef79a2525fd83ecfc22b0983`; every line number above is anchored to the staged checkout because it matches the saved ASan stack.

The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` correspond to broader frame/run-length work and do not patch the reproduced `dict_ddict` lifetime path, so the trace is grounded on the staged vulnerable source plus the saved ASan allocation/free/crash stacks rather than on patch evidence.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not instrument. The saved artifacts establish that a post-free `return -1` is taken from the dictionary-validation block at lines 1693-1705, but they do not disambiguate which exact check in that cluster fired.

coarse_trace.summary: The attacker-controlled `b2frame` is accepted as an in-memory frame-backed super-chunk, and `blosc2_frame_to_schunk()` creates one shared decompression context `schunk->dctx` for later chunk decompressions.
An earlier dictionary-bearing chunk passes dictionary checks and allocates a `ZSTD_DDict` into `schunk->dctx->dict_ddict` from attacker-controlled dictionary bytes.

A later dictionary-bearing chunk frees the existing `dict_ddict` before validating its replacement dictionary, then returns an error from the post-free size-check block before any replacement DDict is installed.

Super-chunk teardown destroys the same shared `dctx`, `blosc2_free_ctx()` frees the stale `dict_ddict` again, and vendored `ZSTD_freeDDict()` rereads `ddict->cMem` from the freed object, matching the saved ASan crash.

fine_trace.note: Source. One earlier dictionary-bearing chunk in the attacker-controlled frame successfully creates a `ZSTD_DDict` from embedded dictionary bytes and stores it in the shared decompression context. The saved allocation stack for the later-crashed 26720-byte region ends at this line.

Root cause. When a later chunk also takes the `BLOSC2_USEDICT` path, the same `initialize_context_decompression()` block frees the previous DDict before validating or replacing the new chunk's dictionary. The field is not cleared after this free.

The later chunk's replacement dictionary is rejected by one of these post-free checks, so control exits `initialize_context_decompression()` before line 1709 can install a new DDict. The staged artifacts do not identify which exact check fires, but they do establish that the function returns after step 2 and leaves `context->dict_ddict` dangling and non-NULL.

depends_on.via: srcsize < sizeof(int32_t) || context->dict_size <= 0 || context->dict_size > BLOSC2_MAXDICTSIZE || srcsize < (int32_t)context->dict_size

fine_trace.note: After decompression stops, super-chunk teardown destroys the same shared decompression context that still carries the stale `dict_ddict` from step 3. This call is in the saved crash stack immediately above `blosc2_free_ctx()`.
Because step 3 left the field non-NULL, cleanup issues a second `ZSTD_freeDDict()` on the same pointer during context destruction.

Sink. The second cleanup free rereads the freed `ZSTD_DDict` object to copy its allocator state. ASan reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 24` at this line, 26696 bytes inside the same 26720-byte region that step 1 allocated and step 2 first freed.

format.name: serialized Blosc2 frame (`b2frame`) for decompress_frame_fuzzer
format.contract: The exact staged 36366-byte `b2frame` witness (SHA-256 `ce607d5fdc9339c56c733094c17277a02d7f9c45eee327c7abd590b7c10cdc56`) must be accepted by `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe()` and decompressed through a shared `schunk->dctx` such that one earlier chunk successfully installs `context->dict_ddict` from an embedded dictionary, and a later `BLOSC2_USEDICT` chunk hits one of the post-free dictionary checks at `blosc/blosc2.c:1693-1705` after line 1690 has already freed the old DDict but before line 1709 can install a replacement. Destroying the `schunk` then re-frees that stale pointer and reaches the saved ASan sink.
